title: Upstream the rest of DOM Parsing and Serialization into HTML

labels.name: topic: xml
labels.description: The XML syntax and parser, DOMParser and XMLSerializer with XML, and XSLT and XPath

body:
At WHATNOT (#13307) there was agreement to finish moving [DOM Parsing and Serialization](https://w3c.github.io/DOM-Parsing/) into HTML and then archive w3c/DOM-Parsing.

Most of it has already moved: `DOMParser` (w3c/DOM-Parsing#60), `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML` and `createContextualFragment` (#10264, #10270, #10282, #10283), and the `XMLSerializer` interface (#11077). What's left is the XML serialization algorithm. It was recently rewritten (w3c/DOM-Parsing#88), so I think it can move mostly verbatim.

Plan:

1. Move the XML serialization algorithm into HTML.
2. Triage the open w3c/DOM-Parsing issues. Close the ones that are fixed or obsolete. For each remaining one, file a new whatwg/html issue that summarizes it, links to the original and cc's its reporter, then close the original with a link to the new issue.
3. Make the published W3C copies point to HTML: redirect https://www.w3.org/TR/DOM-Parsing/ and the dated versions to the HTML Standard, and replace the content of https://w3c.github.io/DOM-Parsing/ with a banner and a meta refresh to the HTML Standard.
4. Archive w3c/DOM-Parsing.

The W3C side is tracked in w3c/DOM-Parsing#93.

cc @lukewarlow
